memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: And you are to love those who are foreigners, for you yourselves were foreigners in Egypt. Fear the Lord your God and serve him. Hold fast to him and take your oaths in his name. He is the one you praise; he is your God, who performed for you those great and awesome wonders you saw with your own eyes. - Deut 10:19-21 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God gives Israel a reason to love the foreigner: "for you yourselves were foreigners in Egypt." They knew from bitter experience what it felt like to be strangers in a land not their own — vulnerable, mistreated, without protection. So God calls them to remember that experience and let it produce compassion. Having received God's rescue and care as strangers, they were to extend the same love to the strangers among them. Love flows out of remembering how we ourselves were treated.

This is a powerful principle for the life of faith. Our own experience of receiving mercy is meant to make us merciful. When we remember where we have been — how we were once helpless and how God cared for us — our hearts soften toward others in similar need. Compassion grows from memory. We love others well when we remember how we ourselves were loved.

This is exactly the logic of the gospel. We were once "foreigners to the covenants of promise" (Eph 2:12), strangers far from God, but Christ brought us near by His blood. Because we have received such undeserved love, we are called to pour it out on others. "Love one another. As I have loved you, so you must love one another" (John 13:34). Remembering how much we have been forgiven and welcomed fuels our love for those still on the outside. Who around you needs the kind of love you yourself have received? Let the memory of God's mercy to you overflow into mercy toward them.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- How does remembering God's mercy to me shape my love for others?
- Who are the "foreigners" or outsiders God is calling me to love?
- Does the memory of being welcomed by God overflow into welcome for others?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, I was once a stranger far from You, but Christ brought me near by His blood. Let the memory of Your undeserved love for me overflow into love for others, especially the outsiders and vulnerable. Help me to love as I have been loved. Amen.
